Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded.

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

According to recent reports, coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

Industry observers note that nearly 72,000 people have been evacuated from areas of Odisha in eastern India as Tropical Cyclone Akvan approaches land. Akvan is expected to make landfall on Friday between Narsapur and Puri, prompting cyclone warnings from the India Meteorological Department for north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts. Peak wind gusts are expected to reach 70mph, with rainfall totals through Friday and Saturday potentially exceeding 200mm for northern coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

After a yellow level 2 severe thunderstorm warning by the South African Weather Service on Tuesday, torrential rainfall and large hail were reported across parts of Johannesburg. The storms triggered flash flooding and caused infrastructure damage in the township of Soweto. One person died, while another remains missing after the severe storms.

It has been revealed that if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Xiaomi introduced a second screen to its flagship phones with last year’s 17 Pros, but didn’t release them outside China. That means the latest 18 Pro and Pro Max are the first chance I’ve had to find out if a screen on the back of a phone is any more useful now than it was when Xiaomi last tried it on 2021’s Mi 11 Ultra — not to mention earlier efforts by the likes of Nubia and Vivo.

Recent findings suggest that after a week or two with both of Xiaomi’s newly introduced Pro phones, I’m not entirely sold. The rear display has a single, obvious use case — it’s helped me take some of the best selfies I’ve ever managed — but it isn’t very useful otherwise.

In a recent development, the rest of the phones are great, with good cameras, major batteries, and a more flexible take on the privacy display seen in the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. There’s a lot to like. But with prices higher than ever thanks to the RAM crisis, it’s hard not to wonder how much buyers are paying for a second screen they could probably do without.

Excellent main and telephoto camerasPrivacy displayStrong performanceCompact.

Industry observers note that there are two Xiaomi 18 Pro phones: the £1,199 Pro (around $1,570) and the £1,399 Pro Max (around $1,830). In the UK and Europe, they’re priced to compete directly with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

They come in similar sizes to the iPhones, too: a 6.4-inch display on the Pro, and 6.9 inches on the Pro Max. There are a few other differences, though not many. The Pro Max’s 7,050mAh battery is bigger than the Pro’s 6,000mAh (with larger batteries available outside Europe), and its 100W wired charging is 10W faster too. Both phones last a day pretty comfortably and will stretch to two with lighter use, though only just — I’ve seen better battery life from recent Oppo and Vivo flagships. They also use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips, though only the Pro Max has the Extreme version. And while the camera setups are nearly identical, you’ll get slightly better dynamic range from the bigger phone thanks to a LOFIC sensor.

The rear screens also vary slightly in size between the phones, though at either 2.7 or 2.9 inches, there’s not much in it. Wrapping around the two main rear camera lenses, they look a lot like the displays you’ll find on the front of foldables like the Galaxy Z Flip 8, though smaller than most of those, and much more limited in functionality.

You can set your choice of wallpapers, some of which are interactive. Listen to music or a podcast, and playback controls appear. You can turn on notifications, useful for when you want to rest your phone face down, but Xiaomi’s implementation is odd: App icons appear so large on the screen that there’s no space to fit much text from a given notification; there are no interactive responses like quick replies or marking emails as read; and you can’t see a list of your notifications, only viewing each for a few seconds as it comes in. It makes this just barely more useful than a notification LED.

According to recent reports, unlike flip phones, you can’t use the small screen to access the phone’s settings, and you certainly can’t run full-blown apps. Instead, there’s a natural-language AI tool to create your own apps, powered by Google’s Gemini 4 Argon. It’s good for simple tools or games — I made a pomodoro timer and a semi-functional knockoff Pac-Man — but your creations can’t connect to the internet or access other apps, so anything you make will be quite purposefully limited.

The only thing that’s convinced me the rear screen is at all worthwhile is its camera viewfinder. The UI’s a little fiddly at this scale, but you can take photos, record videos, or create a photo booth-inspired picture set, all using the rear main camera. I’ve taken the best selfies of my life with this phone, which may be reason enough for some people to buy it.

According to recent reports, it helps that the main camera is especially good. It and the telephoto are both excellent 200-megapixel shooters with large sensors, capable of great results in almost any lighting conditions. The telephoto’s short minimum focusing distance of 12cm lets it double as a great macro camera too. The 18 Pro Max has a slight photographic advantage, with a LOFIC main sensor that offers an expanded 16-stop dynamic range, helping it capture better highlights in particularly tricky lighting. Most of the time you won’t see a huge difference between the two phones.

It has been revealed that xiaomi’s longtime camera partner Leica is involved again, and by default you can shoot in one of two Leica-branded camera modes — Vibrant or Authentic — plus a upcoming third option, the Xiaomi-branded Original, which splits the difference between them. The other big Leica contribution is a new Essential Moments mode that uses AI to simulate three different retro Leica aesthetics in either 35mm or 75mm lenses.

Sources indicate that the ultrawide, set apart from the other two lenses beneath the screen, looks like an afterthought — and it shoots like one too. It’s placed so low on the body that my finger frequently blocks its view; its 17mm focal length barely feels wider than the 23mm main camera, so it doesn’t give you much extra room to play with; and its smaller sensor means quality is noticeably worse than from either of the other rear cameras, especially in dimmer light. As for the selfie camera, it’s decent, but you’ll only ever use it for video calls since the rear screen makes the main camera the better choice the rest of the time.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro phones have one other trick: a privacy display. This is a pretty direct imitation of Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra tech, switching between different sets of pixels with varying viewing angles to make your screen hard to see from the side when it’s activated. Like Samsung’s version, you can turn it on across the phone or just for certain apps; unlike Samsung’s, when you activate it for specific apps, it also applies to specific notifications, and it works with split-screen or floating windows without affecting other apps open at the same time. It’s more flexible than Samsung’s version, though to my eye, less effective.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Pro Max have plenty of strengths, with great main and telephoto cameras, good performance, and reasonably attractive designs. But shortcomings like the lackluster ultrawide camera and batteries that don’t last as long as some rival flagships make me wonder about the compromises made to fit that rear display. Its limited functionality has given me pause, especially as flagship phones like this hit increasingly eye-watering prices.

#70240. Startup sues Apple in India over tap-to-share contacts feature

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (579 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Startup sues Apple in India over tap-to-share contacts feature

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (579 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple is being sued in India by a U.S.-based startup that alleges the iPhone maker’s NameDrop feature, which lets people share contact information by bringing devices close together, infringes its patented technology.
  • GG Technologies, the startup behind StayTouch, an app that lets people exchange contact details by bringing their phones close together, is seeking ₹15 billion (about $161.86 million) in damages and an injunction against Apple, per court documents reviewed by TechCrunch.
  • Santa Monica-headquartered GG Technologies filed the lawsuit in India in October after mediation proceedings initiated in April failed in September, the startup told TechCrunch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is being sued in India by a U.S.-based startup that alleges the iPhone maker’s NameDrop feature, which lets people share contact information by bringing devices close together, infringes its patented technology.

GG Technologies, the startup behind StayTouch, an app that lets people exchange contact details by bringing their phones close together, is seeking ₹15 billion (about $161.86 million) in damages and an injunction against Apple, per court documents reviewed by TechCrunch.

Santa Monica-headquartered GG Technologies filed the lawsuit in India in October after mediation proceedings initiated in April failed in September, the startup told TechCrunch. Pre-institution mediation is generally required before filing commercial lawsuits in India. The firm also sued Apple in the U.S. in April over related patent infringement claims.

In its 781-page court filing in the Bombay High Court, GG Technologies alleged that Apple’s NameDrop infringes its Indian patent on technology that helps phones exchange contact details with nearby devices without requiring manual pairing. The company released StayTouch in 2019, the same year it first sought patent protection for the technology in the U.S. It filed its Indian patent application in 2021 and received the patent in July 2024.

Apple introduced NameDrop as part of iOS 17 in June 2023. The feature debuted on iPhones later that year, with support for compatible Apple Watches arriving in October through watchOS 10.1.

Recent findings suggest that “We are seeking an injunction to restrict the usage of the NameDrop feature which is native to iOS,” GG Technologies told TechCrunch. GG Technologies urged the court in its filing to restrict Apple from selling or importing iPhones and Apple Watches preloaded with NameDrop in India. The case has yet to be listed for a hearing.

In the U.S., the International Trade Commission opened an investigation into Apple’s alleged patent infringement in August, following a complaint from GG Technologies. The startup is seeking an order that could block imports of infringing Apple devices into the country, along with restrictions on their sale.

Founded in 2018 by Gaurav Goel, a graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and a former Goldman Sachs investment banker, GG Technologies developed StayTouch as an alternative to exchanging business cards. The app is available on iOS and Android.

Apple did not respond to a request for comment.

India has become increasingly important to Apple, both as a fast-growing consumer market and a major manufacturing hub outside China. The Cupertino organization has expanded its retail presence in the South Asian nation, where iPhones still account for less than 10% of smartphone shipments, giving considerable room for growth.

Pokemon Gen 10 leaker admits faking rumors, reviving hopes for a new Eeveelution and voice acting

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Pokemon Winds & Waves leaker has admitted to faking rumors about the Gen 10 games, giving fans fresh hope for voice acting and Eevee’s first new evolution in more than a decade.
  • It has been revealed that moot, who posts as @Mootmonthly on X, had built a reputation for sharing information about the Pokemon anime.
  • Meanwhile, a separate account called @kurwashibamaste had been feeding Centro Leaks rumors about the games since July.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Pokemon Winds & Waves leaker has admitted to faking rumors about the Gen 10 games, giving fans fresh hope for voice acting and Eevee’s first new evolution in more than a decade.

It has been revealed that moot, who posts as @Mootmonthly on X, had built a reputation for sharing information about the Pokemon anime. Centro Leaks had publicly vouched for him as a reliable anime source, and his claims about an internal delay for Winds & Waves made it into Dexerto’s November 9 coverage.

Meanwhile, a separate account called @kurwashibamaste had been feeding Centro Leaks rumors about the games since July. It claimed a development build appeared to lack fresh evolutions for Eevee and Tropius. It also claimed voice acting had been planned but had disappeared from recent builds.

On November 17, an X user posted a screenshot appearing to show Moot and @kurwashibamaste in the same account switcher. Moot responded with a GIF captioned “How it feels to spread misinformation and lies.” Centro then said Moot had admitted to running the alternate account and faking many of its Winds & Waves rumors.

Some drama on the Pokémon leak community happening:– @Mootmonthly has admitted to faking a lot of the rumors he started regarding Winds/Waves– Has admitted to being behind the @kurwashibamaste from which a lot of rumors went viral last few months– We now think most of the….

Moot later said he had accomplished a “specific goal” with the account and described keeping up the act as a “larp.” He also said his reputation had made him feel limited in what he could post and that he’d “prefer being viewed as a clown.”.

also honestly? my rep was a little too goodthe dexerto article was neat but having that level of rep kinda forces one into being rather limited in what they can say/posti vastly would prefer being viewed as a clown.

In a recent development, the reveal frustrated fans who had spent months following the rumors. Pokemon creator Light said he had gotten it wrong himself and criticized other accounts for allegedly staying quiet when they suspected what was happening.

Pokemon Winds and Waves reportedly had 2026 launch planned before last-minute delay.

Pokemon Winds and Waves leak reveals map and first look at Grass Gym.

AI Pokemon Winds & Waves “leaks” are fooling fans ahead of Gen 10.

Others were happy to see those rumors fall apart. Pokemon creator SoulSilverArt said a Tropius evolution, a new Eeveelution, and voice acting were “back on the menu.” Eevee’s last new evolution was Sylveon, which debuted in Pokemon X and Y in 2013.

It has been revealed that well there’s some real confirmation, Moot is Kurawashi…Looks Tropius Evo, upcoming Eeveelutions, and VA ARE BACK ON THE MENU BOYS! https://t.co/4chqJMxX6G pic.twitter.com/45M3tN4Yi7.

Recent findings suggest that centro mentioned some real details may have been mixed in. It pointed to the rumor of around 300 new Pokemon and forms as one it had heard separately, adding that development looks could have changed.

The Pokemon Company has yet to announce voice acting or a fresh Eevee evolution. It has confirmed a 2027 release on Nintendo Switch 2 and revealed Gen 10 starters Browt, Pombon, and Gecqua.

It has been revealed that with players finally jumping into Vice City, satire site The Babylon Bee is opening up a city of its own. The game is called Grand Faith Auto, and it takes place in New Mercy, a 3D open world you can explore right in your browser.

The setup will look familiar to anyone who’s played GTA, as there are cars to take, storefronts and billboards dotted around the city, and a radar to help you find your way.

But while the real thing often throws you into the criminal underworld, Grand Faith Auto is all about being an upstanding citizen.

Instead of the traditional Wanted level, doing good deeds earns you stars of divine approval. Get all five, and the devil himself comes looking for you instead of the cops.

One of the deeds you can do around Latest Mercy is pull a driver out of their car and preach to them before driving off in it yourself. You can also offer a “Lady of the Night” a lift to church, or try to feed the hungry in a scenario involving a closed chicken restaurant, a deli under attack, and a box of pocket Bibles.

There’s even a stealth mission where you sneak into a cartel warehouse and swap its drugs for little figurines. You’ll have to stay out of sight, because getting spotted by a guard is an instant fail.

The official Grand Faith Auto game launch trailer. It's the newly introduced hit video game everyone's been waiting to play for years. You’re not completely unarmed, though, as you can wield a holy shotgun to fend off the imps tracking you down. A shot to the head stuns them, leaving you free to kick them back to hell. After that, the instructions tell you to go to church.

Police can’t wait for GTA 6 to be released so they can “catch a break”.

GTA 6 forces you to take your time with the main story instead of speedrunning it.

GTA 6 best guides for launch: Everything you need to know.

That’s probably for the best, given that GTA 6 has already become the joint-best-reviewed game of all time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hershey’s is bringing back its original five-cent chocolate bar price for one day only to celebrate the theatrical release of its newly introduced movie, giving customers several ways to take advantage of the promotion.

The chocolate tech giant is celebrating the November 25 debut of Hershey, a biographical film exploring the lives of Milton Hershey and his wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey, with a limited-time deal inspired by the brand’s history.

The promotion will allow customers to purchase classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bars for just a nickel, matching their original price from 1900. However, the process for claiming the discount varies depending on where customers shop.

The promotion will take place on Wednesday, November 25, with discounted chocolate bars available through Hershey’s Chocolate World, Walmart, and Amazon Grocery.

Customers visiting Hershey’s Chocolate World locations in Hershey, Pennsylvania, or Times Square in New York City can purchase the bars for five cents each beginning at 9 AM local time.

Recent findings suggest that there is a limit of 10 bars per person, and the offer cannot be combined with other discounts. Applicable taxes will still be charged.

According to recent reports, walmart customers can also take advantage of the promotion through two different methods. Those shopping online can purchase a classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bar for five cents by placing an online pickup order through Walmart.com using their Walmart account.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, customers shopping at Walmart stores can receive the discounted price through the Ibotta app. After purchasing a qualifying chocolate bar, shoppers must upload a photo of their receipt to receive cash back.

Walmart’s promotion is limited to five bars per person and does not apply to orders shipped directly to customers’ homes.

Amazon Grocery will also participate in the promotion, offering five-cent chocolate bars through same-day delivery in select markets.

Customers with qualifying delivery addresses can use a promotional code shared through Hershey’s social media channels to receive free shipping at checkout. The offer is limited to two bars per customer while supplies last, with taxes calculated based on the total order.

“The five-cent bar gives fans a chance to experience a sweet piece of Hershey’s story for themselves,” the company said in a statement shared with PEOPLE.

“Bringing it back on the day HERSHEY debuts in theaters gives fans a fun way to celebrate the brand’s roots and the story that inspired it.”.

Alongside the promotion, Hershey’s is introducing vintage-inspired packaging for several products, including its Milk Chocolate Bars and Kisses chocolates.

In a recent development, the packaging features the manufacturer’s historic wordmark, Milton Hershey’s signature, and typography inspired by the brand’s early years. Each package also includes a QR code directing customers to more information about Hershey’s history.

The upcoming movie stars Finn Wittrock as Milton Hershey and Alexandra Daddario as Catherine Hershey, following their relationship and the development of the chocolate manufacturer.

Directed by Mark Waters and filmed in Pennsylvania, the movie also features Alan Ruck, David Costabile, Richard Kind, and several other cast members.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Arizona judge ordered YouTuber Lane Myers released from prison after county prosecutors raised doubts about an email that helped send him there.

Myers, 43, pleaded guilty in July 2025 to felony stalking and harassment charges involving Shannon Walker, the wife of Tucson city prosecutor Matthew Walker. He was placed on probation under conditions that restricted what he could post about the couple.

Sources indicate that in October 2026, Pima County Superior Court Judge Douglas Metcalf sentenced Myers to three years in prison for violating that probation. Prosecutors stated Myers had posted new YouTube videos about the Walkers and argued those videos prompted others to send Shannon Walker threatening and harassing emails.

It has been revealed that investigators tied at least one of those emails to an IP address associated with the Walkers’ home, casting doubt on whether the message came from someone reacting to Myers’ videos. Who sent it remains under investigation.

Deputy County Attorney Rachel Stiles submitted the upcoming evidence under seal and discussed it only in broad terms at the November 17 hearing.

Industry observers note that tucson police searched the Walkers’ home on November 2 and seized several devices, including Matthew Walker’s city-issued laptop. County prosecutors first asked for Myers’ release at an emergency hearing the next day. On November 5, the city of Tucson put Matthew Walker on paid administrative leave while police investigated possible misconduct connected to the probation case.

A Tucson YouTuber was ordered freed from prison after county prosecutors found evidence suggesting the victim or her husband, a city prosecutor, may have drafted harassing emails that helped put him behind bars. https://t.co/An6DVVsuFD.

Recent findings suggest that metcalf returned Myers to probation on November 17, and his 2025 stalking and harassment convictions still stand. Myers thanked county prosecutors in a statement for bringing the evidence forward, and thanked Metcalf for “giving me the opportunity to show I can follow conditions.”.

Stiles mentioned county prosecutors still believe Myers violated his probation and will review the evidence before deciding whether to ask the court to revoke it again. Metcalf scheduled a status hearing for December 8.

Burger King is bringing a massive burger inspired by the Grand Theft Auto franchise into the real world, introducing a seven-patty Whopper based on a fictional fast-food restaurant featured in the games.

The newly introduced creation, called the HeartWhopper, is part of a limited-time promotion from Burger King Belgium that allows GTA fans to win a real version of the oversized burger.

The campaign launches on November 19 and takes inspiration from the fictional fast-food chain found throughout the GTA series, turning one of its recognizable menu items into an actual meal.

The HeartWhopper features seven flame-grilled beef patties stacked with cheese, tomato slices, lettuce, and onion rings, recreating the exaggerated burgers associated with the fictional restaurant.

According to Burger King, the promotion is intended as a parody of the video game franchise’s own parody of fast-food chains, with the company claiming its restaurants have served as inspiration for fictional businesses in gaming.

Rather than introducing the HeartWhopper as a traditional menu item, Burger King Belgium is giving players the chance to win one through a social media competition.

A post shared by Burger King BE & LUX (@burgerkingbe).

To participate, fans must share a video clip showing themselves enjoying a burger from the in-game restaurant and tag either Burger King Belgium or Burger King Luxembourg.

In a recent development, the company will select the most creative submission each day, awarding the winner a real-life HeartWhopper. The competition will run for two weeks, giving players multiple opportunities to participate.

Burger King is also promoting the campaign through YouTube advertisements, YouTube Shorts, and gaming communities on Reddit, with teasers released ahead of the November 19 launch.

You meet Mandy early on in Chapter 1 while making collections for Brian, and, putting it mildly, she has a bit of a soft spot for Jason. She ropes him into fixing her plumbing before he can leave with the cash, only for her to try to seduce him.

It’s a relatively minor moment, and Jason ultimately shoots her down, but social media has been buzzing with fans falling head over heels for Mandy.

Mandy… I'm weak. What have you done Rockstar 😭 pic.twitter.com/mlCsR2NCaQ.

There is one small issue, though — many players are also convinced she’s actually a serial killer.

While fixing Mandy’s sink, Jason removes an object blocking a pipe, which she quickly snatches away from him. However, if you’re looking carefully, you’ll see that it was a severed finger that she’d clearly tried to get rid of.

This is weird enough by itself, but if you take the time to explore the rest of her home, there are even more clues that all is not what it seems.

The trunk of her car contains a number of suspicious items, including a meat cleaver and tape. Meanwhile, you can find containers of acid and saws scattered around her yard.

Most damning of all, there’s even what appears to be a grave at the side of her home, and it looks like it was dug recently, too.

“Isn’t it strange that in a country where people go completely naked in public baths and hot springs, they make people wear swimsuits to take a shower?” wrote one Japanese player.

According to recent reports, “If they’re going out of their way to give it a CERO Z rating for 18+, what’s the point of censoring the content? I don’t get it,” replied another commenter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A high school in Pennsylvania has been forced to scrap a test of AI-powered metal detectors after regular student items were continually flagged as weapons.

Industry observers note that over the last few years, a number of places have updated their security systems, scrapping old metal detectors in favor of newer ones – you’ll have seen them at airports, for example. These up-to-date detectors are supposed to speed up the security process, but they can cause headaches.

That has been the case for the Hempfield Area High School in Pennsylvania, as they have been helping to test the new Wi-AI detection system from CurvePoint AI.

As per TechSpot, Wi-AI uses Wi-Fi signals to look for concealed weapons, with people having to walk near SensePods, which tracks movements without even using cameras.

However, according to WTAE-TV in Pittsburgh, everyday items that students need for school – including binders, water bottles, and batteries – have been routinely flagged as weapons.

“The detection is not what they were hoping to get from the technology side of things and so, we are in agreement that, moving forward, as far as going live, its just not a product that is ready for that activation,” Superintendent Dr. Mark Holtzman told the news outlet.

Skip Smith, the CEO of CurvePoint AI, noted that the school “served as a testing and evaluation site” rather than being a full “operational deployment.”.

Additionally, Holtzman noted that the system was “not near” the 95% accuracy rate that the system hoped to achieve.

Recent findings suggest that it isn’t the first time that similar systems have caused these sorts of headaches. Back in October 2025, a 16-year-old student in Baltimore was swarmed by armed police when an AI gun detection system falsely flagged a Doritos bag as a firearm. That system was shut down just a month later, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Rockstar Games developer says he and his colleagues are worried about losing their jobs after GTA 6, despite the successful launch.

The long-awaited sequel arrived on November 19 to rave reviews, after racking up well over $1 billion in pre-orders, and is likely to be one of, if not the biggest, video game releases ever.

GTA 5 sold more than 230 million copies, and Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte claims the follow-up is expected to surpass it.

But for some of the people who made it, launch week also brings questions about what happens in the weeks and months that follow.

Recent findings suggest that uriarte, who works at Rockstar’s Edinburgh studio, raised those concerns in an opinion piece for The Guardian. He described the pressure game developers have come to expect on either side of a major launch.

“While the highs of a game release like this can be incredible, game workers have also come to expect other, less welcome side effects: intense overtime in the buildup and mass redundancies in the aftermath,” Uriarte wrote.

He pointed to job losses across the games industry to explain why those fears persist, even at Rockstar.

“It states a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.”.

Recent findings suggest that as a result, Uriarte noted he was voting in favor of union recognition because he wants staff to have a say in pay, bonuses, and working conditions. He said Rockstar has already introduced some overtime pay and wants to build on that so workers are paid for every hour they put in.

He went on to admit that there has been no suggestion from Rockstar that layoffs are imminent, but that the fears are still there among staff.

“After the significant day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds,” he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new law from the European Union could impact the way ads from influencers and pay-to-win items in games work, especially those that target minors.

In a recent development, back on November 10, the European Union laid out its first proposal for what they’re calling the Digital Fairness Act. In short, the DFA is looking to clamp down on “unfair commercial practices” that are regularly seen online.

The European Union highlighted things such as “manipulative marketing tactics or hidden fees” as targets of the bill, but they’re also looking at advertisements from influencers too.

In a recent development, while influencers are currently required to use hashtags like ad, sponsored, and gifted on their content, the Digital Fairness Act wants to strengthen that. “Clear disclosure of influencer marketing, requiring influencers to be transparent about commercial content and preventing the exploitation of the trust of minors in their audience,” the EU pointed out as one of the “key” parts of the proposal.

Additionally, pay-to-win and pay-to-progress items in games have also been highlighted as part of the fresh act.

Recent findings suggest that “Fairness by design, with the option for consumers to turn off addictive design features that encourage excessive or compulsive spending, such as persistent prompts. The proposal will also restrict unfair practices that encourage overspending, for example by banning gambling-like features for minors, such as pay-to-win and pay-to-progress,” they added.

It’s unclear as to how broad that anti-pay-to-win protection would be, seeing as there are continual arguments about what can be classified as P2W.

There would also be a crackdown on “fake claims” that tell people to rush to buy items due to apparent low stock and changing prices.

A restaurant in North Carolina has hit out at “miserable and entitled” customers after their rules about tipping went viral on social media, and people thought that the answer would be to review bomb them.

Sources indicate that tipping in restaurants and bar has long been a divisive topic, with different places handling it in their own unique ways. Some establishments put an automatic gratuity charge on bills, while others still leave it up to the customer.

On November 15, the Freeman’s Grub & Pub in Greensboro, North Carolina, come under fire on the EndTipping subreddit after one user flagged a notice about their tipping rules.

According to recent reports, “If our employees have two separate instances of you not tipping well without explanation, we will add a 20% autograt fee on your bill,” the rules state. “Your receipts will be saved if this is the case, and you are welcome to question it,” they also noted, urging customers to leave a name and number if they have any complaints.

The restaurant’s co-owner, Kevin Purcell, responded to the backlash on November 16, noting that he had been hit with review bombs online.

Recent findings suggest that “It is 2026, and you should know by now the rules of engagement and expectations to tip at a bar or restaurant. Our staff is beyond competent; they’re professionals at what they do. You’re expected to tip for the great to excellent service that they provide,” Purcell noted.

GTA 6 screenshot hidden in San Andreas back in 2021 was real and the house has a dark secret

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A mysterious GTA 6 screenshot discovered in San Andreas Definitive Edition back in 2021 has finally been found in Rockstar’s new game, confirming a theory that predates even the infamous 2022 hack.
  • Five years ago, players exploring GTA Trilogy: The Definitive Edition noticed something unusual inside the Lil’ Probe’Inn, a UFO-themed bar in San Andreas.
  • Recent findings suggest that among the photographs on the wall was a picture of a suburban house with palm trees and a UFO flying overhead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mysterious GTA 6 screenshot discovered in San Andreas Definitive Edition back in 2021 has finally been found in Rockstar’s new game, confirming a theory that predates even the infamous 2022 hack.

Five years ago, players exploring GTA Trilogy: The Definitive Edition noticed something unusual inside the Lil’ Probe’Inn, a UFO-themed bar in San Andreas.

Recent findings suggest that among the photographs on the wall was a picture of a suburban house with palm trees and a UFO flying overhead. Unlike the other images, which came from existing Rockstar titles, nobody could identify where it was from.

Dexerto reported on the discovery in November 2021, with fans theorizing that Rockstar had secretly included the first-ever GTA 6 screenshot.

Now, with GTA 6 finally here, it turns out they were right.

The same day the game was released in Fresh Zealand, a player named Jared from the GTA 6 mapping community discovered the house in Belville, located in Leonida’s Leonard County.

The building is almost identical to its 2021 appearance, right down to the garage, palm trees, and surrounding vegetation.

Recent findings suggest that all credit goes to Jared from the GTA VI Mapping server.The house is located in Belville. (https://t.co/hWt1Koz3uz) pic.twitter.com/t2ZsSRPQFI.

However, players who break into the garage will discover something even more bizarre.

Inside is the hideout of a conspiracy theorist who has seemingly figured out that he’s living inside a video game.

Industry observers note that notes scattered around the garage reveal that the resident has been trying to escape Leonida, but can’t purchase a plane ticket to Los Santos or drive beyond the state’s borders. He’s even considering fleeing by boat.

The conspiracy theorist has also noticed NPCs who look identical, neighbors unable to enter their own homes, people glitching through walls, and buildings with nothing behind their locked doors.

GTA Trilogy players think they solved the ‘GTA 6’ house screenshot mystery.

Sources indicate that first GTA 6 screenshot? GTA Trilogy players make substantial discovery in San Andreas.

GTA Online insider indicates “leaked” GTA 6 screenshot mystery will finally be solved soon.

There’s even a graph showing an enormous spike in violent crime alongside numerous references to the number six.

The photo Rockstar added to GTA San Andreas Definitive Edition in 2021 was a real GTA 6 photo.You can visit that house to find more conspiracy theories hidden inside. pic.twitter.com/5vxNFBmsSQ.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps most interestingly, the resident identifies two individuals, known only as J and L, who appear immune to the strange limitations of his world. These are seemingly references to GTA 6 protagonists Jason and Lucia.

We’ll have to see if there’s even more to this discovery as players continue to explore Leonida and see everything the world has to offer.

The find is especially remarkable because the original screenshot surfaced in November 2021, nearly a year before the massive September 2022 Rockstar hack exposed early GTA 6 gameplay.

It’s unclear whether Rockstar planned the garage’s fourth-wall-breaking Easter egg all those years ago or added it after seeing the community obsess over the house.

Either way, the developer managed to hide a glimpse of GTA 6 in plain sight years before its official reveal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

American Airlines has responded after passengers found that their bags had been covered in a brown, liquid-like substance while waiting two hours for them.

Industry observers note that when you get off a flight, there can be a sense of trepidation about what’s to come next. If you land at the wrong time, you’ll be stuck in a long security queue, meaning your bags might end up stuck on the reclaim belt or even taken somewhere else.

Well, for passengers on an American Airlines flight from Miami to Atlanta, they ended up having a two-hour wait for their bags after landing. Yet, that wasn’t the biggest matter.

According to recent reports, as TikToker Derick McCallum, who had been aboard the plane, noted, the bags ended up coming out looking like they’d been covered in poop. “Underneath the flight, it flooded. The doo-doo water got all in the bottom,” McCallum stated. “Now they’re bringing the bags out; there is doo-doo on the bags.”.

The TikToker’s video has racked up more than 1.3 million views, as of writing, with plenty of viewers commenting with their dismay at the claims.

However, an American Airlines spokesperson confirmed that it wasn’t feces on the bags, but rather liquefied peanut butter.

“Unfortunately, a food item from a customer’s checked bag leaked during the flight, affecting several bags nearby,” a spokesperson told the New York Post. “Our team will work directly with the affected customers to make it right.”.

Elsewhere, Delta responded to a flier after they claimed that a flight attendant took a photo of them sleeping and threatened to post it on Facebook.

“The internet is so mean, but I knew Delta would have my back,” TikToker Tasia Jewel stated.

GTA 6 fans are discovering that driving while checking their in-game phone drastically changes the way their vehicle handles, spawning a wave of viral memes and videos that highlight how dangerous it is.

Driving while looking at your mobile phone is never a good idea, as it drastically impairs your ability to react to your surroundings and can even lead to fatal accidents.

This alone isn’t the only danger to any unfortunate NPC that happens to stray into your general direction, but the car also becomes noticeably harder to control. In fact, it feels like fighting with your controller when it comes to making those smooth maneuvers.

In a recent development, as you can imagine, it’s not exactly the optimal way to drive, especially if you want to keep your car from becoming a total wreck or avoid any pedestrian-related accidents. Well, unless you’re after some run-ins with the cops (it is a GTA game after all).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 players have discovered Dexter Morgan’s apartment in Vice City, complete with a collection of his signature killing tools and even a boat resembling the one used by the TV serial killer.

Back in August, fans spotted what appeared to be Dexter’s apartment in GTA 6 after Rockstar released its 26-minute extended gameplay showcase.

The building closely resembled the real-life Miami apartment complex used throughout the original eight seasons of Dexter, but fans had no way of knowing whether Rockstar had included any additional references.

Now that GTA 6 has released, players have tracked down the waterfront property and uncovered a number of Easter eggs that make the connection even clearer.

As shown in footage shared by DETONATED, players can explore the complex, which Rockstar has named “Trinity Apartments.”.

That’s a reference to the infamous Trinity Killer, Arthur Mitchell, who was played by John Lithgow in Dexter Season 4 and remains one of the show’s most iconic villains.

Dexter Easter Eggs in Grand Theft Auto 6 🔥💥 Dexter's Apartment at 'Trinity Apartments'💥 'Slice of Life' Boat💥 Tools on Roof including SyringeLocated on Washington Island (Vice Beach) pic.twitter.com/q8lnAMR3rH.

Although players can walk right up to Dexter’s apartment door, they can’t actually enter the property. There is an air conditioner, though, an ideal place for hiding blood slides.

However, those who make their way onto the roof will discover something much more sinister.

In a recent development, hidden on top of the building is what appears to be one of Dexter’s signature kill kits, containing a knife, tape, rope and a syringe. These are all tools the serial killer famously used to subdue and murder his victims throughout the series.

The references don’t end there, either. Nearby, players can find and steal a Lure Predator L35P, a boat resembling Dexter’s beloved “Slice of Life.”.

GTA 6 fans convinced they already found a Dexter Easter Egg in Vice City.

GTA 6 best guides for launch: Everything you need to know.

GTA 6 gameplay, map, radio, and cutscene leaked ahead of Netflix Extended Look.

According to recent reports, in the show, Dexter regularly used the Slice of Life to transport and dispose of his victims’ remains in the ocean. While the GTA 6 vessel doesn’t carry the same name, players can take it out onto the water and recreate some of the Bay Harbor Butcher’s infamous trips.

It’s an impressive tribute to the series, especially given that Rockstar hasn’t explicitly identified the location as Dexter’s home.

With GTA 6 only just launching, players have already begun uncovering secrets across Leonida. Fans previously spotted a Vice City Easter egg hiding in the game’s trailer, and there are likely plenty more discoveries waiting to be made.

Umamusume: Pretty Derby is teaming up with the Denver Broncos for their clash against the Miami Dolphins, bringing Gold Ship and Mejiro McQueen to the NFL in specially designed uniforms.

From appearing at the Grand Prix de Paris to being plastered across a BMW in Japan’s Super GT championship, Umamusume’s anime horse girls have been sighted at a lot of sports events this year.

While the Seattle Seahawks previously shared Umamusume-inspired fan art on social media, the Denver Broncos are taking the crossover further with an official collaboration that brings both Gold Ship and Mejiro McQueen to their stadium for the December 6 game.

During the game at Empower Field at Mile High, Umamusume will appear on the stadium’s screens and horseshoe-shaped LED ribbon.

Fans attending the game could also find themselves on an Umamusume-themed fan cam, you know, just in case you were worried there weren’t enough horse girls in your soccer game.

There’s even going to be life-size cutouts of Gold Ship and Mejiro McQueen available for photos at a booth near Gate 8. Visitors can collect a postcard featuring the pair and a rally flag showing Gold Ship’s touchdown, with both illustrations specifically created for the event.

It’s vital to note that you don’t need a game ticket to visit the Umamusume booth or receive the giveaways, but you will need one to watch the Denver Broncos take on the Miami Dolphins inside the stadium.

The booth opens at 11:05 a.m. MST on December 6 and closes at 2:05 p.m., when the Broncos’ Week 13 game kicks off.

A woman has revealed that she completed seven marathons in 2026 despite being pregnant for a few of them, admitting that it was a bit “bizarre” at times.

For a lot of people, running a marathon is a goal that they work towards for months, if not years. Some want to set an impressive time, while others just want to be able to say they’ve completed the 26.2 miles.

In the case of Deirdre Keane, the 38-year-old is a seasoned long-distance runner, completing more than 60 marathons to this point. However, throughout 2026, she has been running marathons with an additional hurdle to deal with: she has been pregnant throughout.

“I knew how bizarre it was to be running a marathon at 34 weeks, but I also knew how fit I was and self-aware of my body at this point,” she told the Associated Press, admitting it is a “very unusual” challenge, but noted that she isn’t the first woman to do so.

As per the AP, the 38-year-old had signed up for 11 races in 2026, including the seven major marathons: Berlin, Boston, Chicago, London, New York, Sydney and Tokyo.

“I was like, this is going to be my last hurrah before settling down and becoming pregnant, becoming a mother,” Keane added. However, she didn’t discover she was pregnant until after running the Tokyo marathon, when she noticed her pace had started to slip.

“I don’t think she thought I would do them towards the end, especially being so pregnant at Upcoming York. But I am very stubborn and determined,” Keane added. “Plus, I got lucky; I was feeling good. So I was able to do it.”.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick is already being asked about GTA 7, despite GTA 6 only being days old.

Rockstar released GTA 6 on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait for a new numbered Grand Theft Auto.

But while players are only just getting their first look at Vice City and the rest of Leonida, some are already looking ahead to the next entry in the series.

On launch day, Zelnick joined the TBPN podcast to talk about the release, and was asked early on about when GTA 7 could drop, to which he answered: “Once you get through several hundred hours of the most incredible fun you’ve ever heard, ask the question again.”.

Later in the interview, he was asked about the sequel again and how big the map could be, given that GTA 6 covers a huge city and a surrounding state.

“Theoretically, GTA 7 could just be a live version of the entire world, right?” one of the hosts asked, with Zelnick clearly amused by the question.

“We at Take-Two just went live with GTA 6 on November 19,” he jokingly replied. “Let me check my watch. Oh, it’s still November 19. And you’re asking a question about GTA 7. I mean guys, really?”.

According to recent reports, jordi: "Theoretically, GTA 7 could just be a live version of the entire world, right?"@StraussZelnick, the CEO behind GTA 6: "We went live with GTA 6 on November 19. He then mentioned a quote his father used to say about past achievements being “yesterday’s headlines,” but then quipped: “It’s not even yesterday.”.

Recent findings suggest that with GTA 6 only just arriving, it will likely be years before we get any concrete information about its potential follow-up. However, Zelnick has hinted that Rockstar’s future games won’t take as long to make.

Plus, we still have GTA 6 Online to look forward to, which should tide players over until GTA 7.

A brand-new phone that doesn’t connect to the internet has been released in Japan, and it looks like the classic Nokia phones that you might remember.

For years, smartphone people have been trying to find creative solutions to cut down their screen time, especially as phones have started doing weekly reviews of app usage and screen time.

Some have opted to set time limits on the apps they can use, while others have created heavyweight cases that will quite literally force you to work out in order to use your smartphone.

It has been revealed that in other cases, some people have taken a step back in time, ditching their smartphones for flip phones and devices that don’t actually connect to the internet. These throwback phones have popped up across Europe and the United States, and now Japan is getting in on the act with a new device.

As per The Japan Times, Japan’s KDDI Corporation has introduced a mobile phone with “minimal functions.”.

Sources indicate that named the Infobar Zero, it will be available to pick up on Christmas Day, and is limited to calls, text messages, and other basic features. Owners won’t have the ability to connect to the internet, but it will have a camera and a music player.

While it isn’t a complete recreation of Nokia’s iconic 3310 phone, the Infobar Zero does strike up plenty of comparisons to that classic device.

Additionally, the ‘dumbphone’ isn’t aimed at replacing your smartphone, but rather providing a break from the smartphone life.

It has been planned by KDDI for quite some time, just as a way of relieving the reliance to live life on apps.

Owners will be able to register their phone numbers on the Zero and a smartphone as part of KDDI’s “two numbers” system – sort of like using an eSIM in some parts of the world.

While many GTA 6 fans across PlayStation and Xbox are enjoying their time in Leonida, it’s not all sunshine and rainbows for everyone trying to explore Rockstar’s latest installment.

Since its November 19 release, players have reported game-breaking crashes that prevent them from progressing through the main story and even playing altogether.

In a Reddit post, one PS5 player said the game had worked flawlessly until they reached Pipework, one of the game’s early missions, where you are introduced to Mandy.

According to recent reports, “Game keeps crashing at the exact same point during the opening prologue. I’m using a PS5 Pro and have been unable to play since launch. The game crashes immediately as the startup prologue begins, either at the exact same point or a couple of seconds into it, displaying error code CE-108255-1.”.

Recent findings suggest that when checking the PlayStation Support page, error CE-108255-1 prompts players to simply “try updating your game”. However, GTA 6 fans who have encountered this issue on PS5 have reported that clearing the console’s cache, rebuilding its database, factory resetting the PS5, and downloading the game three times has done nothing to alleviate the problem.

Recent findings suggest that the reports are not limited to PlayStation, either, as some Xbox Series X players have also reported crashes within minutes of play. “The game sometimes even crashes after only 15 minutes. It has been revealed that animal control was forced to respond to a call about an alligator on the loose, but it turned out to be just a pool floatie. Seriously.

Over the years, plenty of people have rushed to call emergency services to report something that, when investigated, turned out to be totally false.

This was the case over in Sugar Land, Texas, on November 12 when animal control received a call about an alligator being on the loose. As per Sugar Land Animal Services, they were told that the gator appeared to be feeling a bit sick and in need of some assistance.

Yet, when they reached it, it wasn’t all it seemed. “When ASO Perez arrived on the scene to investigate, she was in for a big surprise. What looked very real from a distance turned out to be a runaway pool floatie!” they posted on Facebook.

“While this call definitely gave our team a good laugh, we always take every report seriously,” Animal Services added.

In the photo, the inflatable gator had its mouth stuck open with teeth on show, so if you see it from a distance, you might be confused. However, up close, you can tell it’s meant to be lounged on, not hunted or scared of.

Sources indicate that “Remember: if you ever spot wildlife that looks sick or injured, please keep a safe distance and call the experts to handle it. You never know if it’s the real deal!”.

Industry observers note that naturally, commenters saw the funny side of things too. “Well, that was a rather inflated story then,” one joked. “She is very brave! Thank you, Officer Perez, for all you do,” another added. “Wow. It looks so realistic! Crazy,” another replied.

As noted, it isn’t the first instance of floaties being reported as real, nor is it the wildest.

Good morning. Plus, prayers to anyone who had to find a last-minute hotel room during last week’s flying nightmare.

Industry observers note that inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

It has been revealed that in the immediate fallout of Jensen Huang’s humiliating resignation from Nvidia, coverage will focus on how the company looks to continue without its beloved former CEO, the world’s biggest champion of open-source AI and the proliferation of GPUs across borders. But in the long term, there’s an argument to be made that Google will be one of the largest winners of the shake-up, with a market opening up to competition outside of Nvidia’s CUDA moat.

While Colette Kress, the interim CEO, is unlikely to make any drastic changes to the company’s roadmap, the reality is that Nvidia’s competitors in the semiconductor space have desperately been working to unseat the market leader, and without Jensen at the helm, customers may be more likely to pursue alternatives.

According to recent reports, for years, Google has offered its TPUs, or Tensor Processing Units, as a solution for AI training and inference, but they’ve been largely locked to its Google Cloud infrastructure. That’s changing now that the company is opening up sales to third parties and has declared it will bring TPU capacity to Oracle’s cloud beginning in 2027.

Google’s latest generation of TPUs is specialized; here’s how the company describes the lineup in its recent announcement post:.

In a recent development, while flexible across workloads, together the four systems in our eighth-generation TPUs give customers a purpose-built accelerator for every stage of the agentic lifecycle. TPU 8t for scale-up training, TPU 8i for low-latency reasoning (inference), TPU 8tx for confidential computing, and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack.

Google isn’t comparing its upcoming TPUs directly to Nvidia’s offerings, and clock-for-clock, even the most powerful TPU 8i Max doesn’t touch Vera Rubin for sheer performance. But this generation should be much more competitive for a few reasons: it’s more power efficient in certain configurations, and Google made it easier to translate coding workflows optimized for CUDA to work with its TPUs.

Back in October, Google open-sourced TorchTPU, which it co-developed with Meta’s PyTorch team, to let developers use familiar PyTorch workflows on TPUs with minimal code changes. That won’t make every custom CUDA operation portable or eliminate performance tuning, but reducing the effort required to try an alternative may change the buying decision. Customers don’t need to abandon Nvidia outright for Google to increase its TPU market share, or for Nvidia to face more pressure on price.

Alongside Broadcom and MediaTek, Google is taking on the Nvidia behemoth, and in the short term, it will almost certainly see a large upside in sentiment. But in the longer term, with scaling pressure lowering margins for Nvidia, Google’s specialized and more efficient TPUs may be a primary beneficiary of this sea change. They could also offset a slowdown in Search as Google’s shift to Cloud continues apace.

Android Time Machine is an extremely vibe-coded experience, but once you get past the bad vibes, the ability to play around with some of the earliest versions of Android in your phone’s browser becomes magical pretty promptly.

Over the past few days, the one-two punch of Microsoft’s 365/Exchange outage and the FAA’s ground stop indicates just how vulnerable everyone is to the effects of seemingly brittle tech infrastructure.

In a recent development, the FAA describes a flood of connection attempts that destabilized its telecommunications network, affecting aircraft communications and radar feeds. Investigators identified sites in Arkansas and Texas that were undergoing router and wire replacements, but even days after the stop was lifted, there’s still no clear underlying cause.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the Microsoft 365 outage lasted about 30 hours, with service restored to the remaining customers and regions late Friday. Microsoft states that a “latent defect” introduced into its network code in a July update wasn’t triggered until a few days ago, when high loads led to cascading failures across the company’s servers worldwide.

While neither AI nor cyberattacks were to blame, individually and together the two outages add urgency to getting companies to shore up their defenses and redundancies in a world where we’re overly reliant on digital systems.

Finally, if you’re into DIY projects, you’ve likely heard of TRMNL, the manufacturer that makes very cool and slightly overpriced ePaper displays that can be programmed to do basically whatever you want with them.

Now, the company has just revealed a 31.5-inch color ePaper version, encased in a custom wood frame, that sells for nearly $2,000. It can be mounted on a wall without internet, using a microSD card and a 20,000mAh battery, for months of gorgeous art displays, or kept powered and connected to the internet to be used as a (very large) home dashboard.

I want one very badly, but I’ve already chosen my $2,000 poison.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chipotle is bringing back its Thanksgiving BOGO promotion, giving customers a chance to score a free meal ahead of the holiday.

The fast food chain unveiled on November 20 that its Back Home BOGO deal will return for one night only, allowing Rewards members to get two meals for the price of one at participating US restaurants.

The promotion first released in 2025 and became Chipotle’s largest sales-driving campaign of the year. Its return comes as millions of Americans prepare to travel home and reconnect with friends and family over Thanksgiving weekend.

On Wednesday, November 25, Chipotle Rewards members can receive a free meal when purchasing another one of equal or greater value between 5 p.m. and 9 p.m. local time.

To redeem the offer, customers must visit a participating US Chipotle restaurant and scan their Rewards membership card at checkout.

The promotion is available exclusively in restaurants, meaning orders placed through the Chipotle app, website, delivery services, or third-party platforms will not qualify.

It has been revealed that customers can receive up to five free meals per check, provided they purchase an meal of equal or greater value for each free item. Kids’ meals do not count toward the promotion.

“Thanksgiving Eve is when the hometown group chat comes to life,” mentioned Stephanie Perdue, Chipotle’s Senior Vice President of Brand Marketing.

“Whether Chipotle is the first stop of the night or where the crew ends up later, we’re giving friends a place to get together over real food. The response last year demonstrated us how much our guests embraced the occasion, and we’re excited to bring it back as another reason for hometown crews to reconnect before Thanksgiving.”.

Chipotle is giving away free food to anyone with a tattoo for one hour only.

Chipotle is offering $6 entrees on Halloween to customers who wear costumes.

Chipotle rolls out School Spirit BOGO with free entrees for back-to-school season.

The tech giant cited Morning Consult research showing that 76% of Gen Z consumers visit restaurants to socialize with friends and family, highlighting the role dining out plays in holiday gatherings.

Chipotle is also offering a separate promotion following Thanksgiving, giving customers a $0 delivery fee on qualifying orders from November 27 through November 30.

Recent findings suggest that to claim the delivery offer, customers must enter the code CYBER26 when ordering through Chipotle’s app or website. The deal requires a minimum purchase of $10 in the US or $12 in Canada, excluding taxes and fees.

Although the delivery fee will be waived, customers may still face higher menu prices and additional service fees.

Both promotions are available for a limited time at participating locations, with the Thanksgiving BOGO ending at 9 p.m. local time on November 25.

  • Through the SIM Manager app on Android, the folks over at Android Authority noticed strings that tell a pretty clear story.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Similar to a recent iPhone feature, Google appears to be working on “Fast Switch” as a way to share one SIM and phone number on two Android phones at once, and it sounds pretty cool.

Through the SIM Manager app on Android, the folks over at Android Authority noticed strings that tell a pretty clear story.

A newly introduced feature called “Android Fast Switch” would let you “use your phone number on up to two phones,” with the SIM automatically switching to “whichever phone you unlock.”.

“Android Fast Switch” sounds nearly identical to Handoff on iPhone, a feature that lets iPhone owners share one SIM between two iPhones and quickly switch devices on the fly.

Recent findings suggest that other strings explicitly say that you can “Use a SIM on two phones” and specify that both devices would need to be logged into the same Google account. One phone would be the “Primary” with the other as a “companion.”.

Sources indicate that there are still plenty of unknown details here, including what data might sync between devices as well as how carriers will respond. On iPhone, carriers either charge extra for this feature ($5 at T-Mobile, $10 at Verizon), or don’t support it at all (AT&T). We also don’t know what devices may be supported – this could easily end up as a Pixel-only affair.

This would make my decision to buy device like Clicks Communicator much easier.

As per usual with these early teardowns, though, the actual launch of a feature like this could be weeks, months, or even years away. Still, the idea itself is rather exciting.

In a recent development, iPhone’s Handoff feature always sounded useful, but I personally always questioned why it would be useful on iPhone. With so little variety in hardware, the utility of switching between two iPhones seems somewhat dubious, outside of perhaps using a Mini or Air as a situational device alongside a Pro device.

On Android, the combinations are endless. It all just depends on what devices Google supports. What devices would you switch between?

#70098. XREAL Aura Initial Review: Taking Android XR out of the headset, but who is it for?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2332 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5google ↗ Open Full Page

XREAL Aura Initial Review: Taking Android XR out of the headset, but who is it for?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2332 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we all kind of want to be Tony Stark, don’t we?
  • XREAL isn’t new to the mixed reality space.
  • There are the glasses themselves which include two displays, one for each eye, and electrochromic dimming on the lenses to control just how much of the outer world you’re seeing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we all kind of want to be Tony Stark, don’t we? Almost everyone can relate to that futuristic sense of wonder that comes from the movies where we see digital elements being interacted with through a simple wave of the hand. To date, that’s only really been replicable through significant ol’ headsets like Apple’s Vision Pro or the various Meta Quest sets. But with XREAL Aura, Android XR brings that feeling to something far easier to actually use, but my one remaining question is who this product is for.

XREAL isn’t new to the mixed reality space. The company has been building some of the best example of optical see-through XR glasses. These aren’t quite like a VR headset because they actually let you see the world around you, not through a camera, but by simply making the lenses themselves see-through. I’ve tried these in the past and, while they’re great for mirroring a tablet or laptop for bigger screen (especially on airplanes), I did feel they were missing something.

But first, let’s talk hardware.

XREAL Aura is a two-part device. There are the glasses themselves which include two displays, one for each eye, and electrochromic dimming on the lenses to control just how much of the outer world you’re seeing. It’s wildly different from a typical VR headset, while also having most of the same benefits. Unlike most other XREAL glasses, Aura has built-in world-facing cameras used for hand and spatial tracking, as well as being able to be used as a camera for things like scanning QR codes, Gemini Live, or simply taking a quick picture (there’s no privacy light here, but the bulkier-than-normal design compared to standard glasses is more than enough a dead giveaway that the “perv glasses” dilemma doesn’t really apply in my opinion).

The other half of the formula is a wired puck that provides battery power and the brains of Android XR. There’s no screen on the puck, just a status light, and it has USB-C out for the glasses as well as USB-C in for power and/or external devices. It also has a fingerprint sensor (are you hearing this Android tablet makers??) and a touchpad, the latter used as a secondary, far subtler input method within Android XR to supplement hand tracking.

In a recent development, together, these two make a wonderful package for building a true mixed reality experience. The displays are plenty bright for even the brightest indoor conditions (frankly, it’d be insane to use these outside in my opinion, though a wide-open plane window may present a challenge), and the electrochromic dimming does a great job of blocking out most, but not quite all of the world around you. If you’re looking to be fully cut off from reality as you would with a VR headset, these aren’t for you. I did find some display elements, like smaller text, a little tough to focus my eyes on at times, but I have a feeling that’s more so me being overdue for an eye exam than it is the glasses themselves. There’s virtually no flicker in my usage, with only bright white backgrounds occasionally being a little overbearing, and everything is smooth with the 120Hz refresh rate.

Where this hardware really shines compared to a typical VR headset is in its design, and it’s what makes XREAL a perfect partner for Android XR. The glasses themselves weigh in at 95 grams, a mere fifth of the Meta Quest 3 and Samsung’s Galaxy XR, and up to 700 grams less than Apple’s Vision Pro. It’s comfortable for much longer periods of time and not nearly as annoying to actually put on either, as it just feels like putting on a pair of bulky sunglasses. They look a little goofy, obviously, but far less so than a full-on VR headset like any of those mentioned above. This is also the only one of those I consider “mixed reality” thanks to the see-through lenses. Apple and Samsung constantly talk about Vision Pro and Galaxy XR as if they’re mixed reality, but a camera feed is explicitly not true reality. But XREAL’s glasses still aren’t quite just augmented reality, because they’re not just letting you see that digital world through a tiny window, they’re quite literally overlaying everything on top of the real world around you. The illusion is somewhat broken by the limited 70-degree field-of-view and the fact that darker backgrounds often look a little funky when there are light sources in the real world in front of you, but I can say with confidence that this is my favorite version of this experience – the speakers are pretty good too, topping it all off.

And that brings us to Android XR.

Google’s platform debuted on Samsung’s Galaxy XR headset earlier this year, and it’s all pretty familiar on XREAL Aura. The Android-based experience opens up to a floating launcher of your favorite apps that mostly open up into floating windows in front of you. You can use hand gestures to move everything around or interact with UI elements, and every app I tried worked perfectly well. The gestures can be hit or miss at times, especially the one for going back to the home screen (having this as a long-press that you have to physically look at your hand for gets annoying when doing anything remotely fast-paced, but thankfully the top button is a dedicated home shortcut), but it works well and everything is designed fairly intuitively. A floating cursor shows where you are aiming with a pinch acting as a tap on a touchscreen, and you can move things around in your space as if they’re real objects. There’s a sense of depth throughout the entire experience.

Some apps open to fully immersive experiences, but these are still in the minority. XREAL touts that there are around 150 experiences launching alongside Aura, but it’s definitely still early days here. Apps like Google TV should obviously be ready for a full format like that but, most things, like the Google Docs app which I’m typing this review in right now, just act as if they’re on independent displays floating around you.

Sources indicate that like Googlebook, Android XR is also still struggling to figure out the best app experience for each user. Most things are mobile apps, including Google Chrome which is just the standard Android version from your phone. It’s fine in most cases, but I found this restrictive seeing as I can get a ton done in a browser, but fighting mobile optimization is a frustrating way to interact with a window that can be as massive as a TV if you want it to. Meanwhile, the Spotify app is weirdly the web version which is horribly optimized for interacting with hand gestures. I’d have rather had the mobile version here. Another quirk I found was notifications, which pop up at the top of the display and quite literally on top of whatever you’re doing. Something they were invasive, and having to physically reach out to dismiss them is a little annoying. I’m sure there are workflows to help make this less of a distraction, but I’d almost rather have notifications turned off entirely.

There’s also Gemini, which is core to the experience here. A quick “Hey Google” triggers a Gemini Live session for answering questions, and you can share what you’re seeing to give additional context. It’s way faster than switching between apps to get a quick search done, but there are friction points here, especially if you’re just asking a single question. Gemini answers quickly and leaves the conversation going, great for follow-up queries, bad if you’re done because the UI controls go away, which leaves you to tell Gemini to end the session which, every time, it asks for secondary confirmation you want to end. Google, if I say “end the session,” I think that should be more than sufficient proof I want to end the session. Luckily, a long-press of the top home button fixes that headache, but I still hate that I either need to use a physical control, or basically have to fight an AI to end a conversation that I started hands-free.

Performance is excellent. Everything is smooth and quick, probably thanks in part to XREAL’s use of 12GB of RAM alongside Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite chip.

But how do you actually use a product like this?

That’s the question I found myself asking when I first spun up XREAL Aura and started to learn its ins and outs. See, other XREAL glasses have an extremely straightforward use case. Plug in the external device of your choice, get it on a bigger screen. Simple, easy, obvious. I found this helpful in travel primarily, with a bigger display for my MacBook feeling nice for tasks like video editing, while the main value came in just having a very comfortable way to watch a movie on a flight from my connected tablet.

Recent findings suggest that both of those use cases are valid on XREAL Aura. You can plug a USB-C device into the puck to get that wired mirroring through an Android XR window, and it works super well. Having Android XR alongside that mirroring also opens the door to added functionality, like having extra windows off to the side for perhaps a media app or reference document if you run out of room on the wired device. As just one example, I kept Spotify and Slack open in side windows while using Aura with my MacBook Air for an afternoon of writing articles.

Recent findings suggest that I think Android XR makes Aura an absolute powerhouse for media consumption, as you can just download content directly to the device (256GB of storage in the base model) for a flight, or even just use streaming apps if you have Wi-Fi. I couldn’t find any 3D content during my brief review period (nothing in my Google TV library was compatible, apparently), but that’s also on the table. Genuinely, I cannot wait to use these on my next long flight.

But outside of those, I think a lot of the other scenarios start to fall apart.

By far the most popular use case for virtual/mixed reality has been gaming. XREAL Aura has a ton of potential here and I’m really excited to try out Project Hail Mary: Journey to the Stars on this, but the fact that these are simply glasses restricts a lot of what you can do. Any massive movements could easily result in the glasses slipping or even falling off, whereas a VR headset is much more secure. Stationary immersive gaming has potential, and XREAL’s Gamesir controller collab indicates promise, but I’m just not sold on these as a replacement to something like Meta Quest seeing as the latter already has a deep catalog of games and a much more affordable price.

The other use case is productivity, one I’m also not entirely sold on. As mentioned, this entire post was written in Aura, and I’m not sure I benefitted much from that experience versus just using a normal laptop or desktop computer. My workflow was having Google Docs up in the center, typing on a physical keyboard (only a psycho could use the virtual keyboard for anything beyond the shortest messages or passwords) with reference documents in Chrome off to my right and Slack on my left, with the occasional “Hey Google” command helping to find information on the fly (such as the weight comparison earlier). It all works well, but I think Android XR is inherently limited by its reliance mostly on mobile apps, and also just by the use of gestures. You can use a mouse or trackpad, of course, but at that point you might as well just use a laptop.

XREAL Aura is for a very specific customer from my point of view. Wired mirroring is still very much the strong suit here, with Android XR’s apps and offline video giving these utility outside of just relying on another device. That was my problem with previous XREAL glasses, because the experience just varies wildly depending on what’s connected. Aura’s puck and Android XR experience solves every complaint I had about previous models, while expanding very much on what it can do.

Further limiting matters is the price. $1,279, in my book, is actually a mostly fair price for this, especially given the RAMageddon of it all. XREAL 1+ Pro come in around $600 and is utterly useless without a secondary device. XREAL Aura more or less doubles the price, but includes the best possible version of that secondary device while also giving you the added camera sensors that are only available as add-ons for other hardware. Don’t get me wrong, it’s still pricey, but I don’t think it’s unfair either, especially not when one of the main competitors for this sort of experience is still $3,600 (which still sounds insane two years later, even for Apple).

We’ll have far more to say about XREAL Aura in a long-term review from our Nick Sutrich, but the verdict on day one is that Android XR has really solved the biggest problem for XREAL, while XREAL has solved a lot of massive problems for Android XR, all while being an overall win for the user at the end of the day. Not so often we get a storybook ending like that in tech anymore, and I’m all here for it.

In a recent development, don’t forget, XREAL Aura is $200 off – so $1,099 – through the end of December. Much more worth it at that price.
